=================== this data base begins from this line ======================

Test Case: Heat transfer of fully developed turbulent channel flow with 
iso-thermal walls

Date of Release:  JANUARY, 2001

Computors:     O. Iida and N. Kasagi
                Department of Mechanical Engineering
                The University of Tokyo
                Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo 113

Nomenclature:

Cf	        = friction coefficient, Cf = 2tau_w/(rho x <U>**2)
cp		= specific heat at constant pressure
d		= interval from the wall to the maximum velocity location
k		= turbulent kinetic energy, u_i x u_i/2
Nu		= Nusselt number, 2q_w x d/(<T>-T_w)/lambda
Pr		= molecular Prandtl number
p		= pressure
q		= heat flux
Re_b		= Reynolds number, 2U_b x delta/nu
Re_tau		= Reynolds number, u_tau x delta/nu
T 		= temperature
t		= temperature fluctuation
t_mean		= arithmetic mean temperature
T_h 		= temperature at the heated wall
T_c		= temperature at the cooled wall
T_tau		= friction temperature on each wall, q_w/rho/cp/u_tau
DT 		= temperature difference between the two walls, Th - Tc
U, V		= mean velocities
U_c		= channel center mean velocity
U_b		= bulk mean velocity
u, v, w  	= velocity components in the x-, y- and z-directions
u+, v+, w+	= u/u_tau, v/u_tau, w/u_tau
u_tau		= friction velocity on each wall
x, y, z 	= streamwise, wall-normal and spanwise coordinates; y = 
-1.0 and y = 1.0 at the heated
		  and cooled walls, respectively
y+		= y x u_tau/nu
delta		= channel half width
lambda		= thermal conductivity
nu		= kinematic viscosity
rho		= density
tau_w		= wall shear stress averaged on two walls
( )_rms		= root-mean-square value
( )_w		= wall value
( )+		= normalized by the wall variables on each wall
< >	        = bulk-averaged quantity over d
t+		= t/t_tau



1. Description of Flow Field

The flow field simulated is a fully developed two-dimensional turbulent flow
between two parallel vertical walls.  The walls are assumed to be kept at 
different,
but constant temperatures without fluctuations.  The flow field is 
homogeneous both
in the streamwise and spanwise directions and the statistics are dependent 
only upon
the distance from the wall.  The data presented here are non-dimensionalized
by the wall variables,i.e., u_tau and nu.  The flow condition is defined by 
the pressure
gradient imposed (or the friction velocity) and the temperature difference 
between the walls.

2. Numerical Method

Governing equations:  a forth-order equation for v, a second-order equation
for omega_y derived from the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the
Boussinesq approximation, the continuity equation, and the energy equation.

Discretization method:  spectral method = 128 x 128 Fourier series in the x-
and z-directions, and Chebyshev polynomials up to the order 97 in the y-
direction (Chebyshev-tau method).

Aliasing treatment: nonlinear terms computed with collocation grids 1.5 times
finer in each direction.

Grid spacing:  18.4 and 7.36 viscous units in the x- and z- directions and
0.08〜4.9 in the y-direction.

Time integration: second-order Adams-Bashforth scheme for the nonlinear terms
and Crank-Nicolson scheme for the viscous terms.

Size of computational box:  (5 pai x delta) x (2 delta) x (2 pai x delta).

Initial conditions: u', v' and u_mean given in accordance with the previous
numerical results.

Boundary conditions: ordinary non-slip condition was imposed on the u and w
components at the walls. The two walls were assumed to be kept at different
but constant temperatures without fluctuations.

Criterion for stationary state: linear profile of total stress and stationary
behavior of mean velocity and second-order moments of the three velocity
components at some distance from the wall.

Length of time integration for ensemble averaging: 120 nu/u_tau**2 (1000 
time steps)
in the flow and thermal fields after the fully developed state is reached.

Error in continuity equation = Max [abs {div(roh*v)} ] : not applicable

Courant number = Max [ delta-t * {abs(u_i/delta-x_i)} ] :  < 0.3

Computer:  HITAC-S820/80 at the Computer Center of the University of Tokyo.

Computation time:  about 3.2 sec CPU time per one time step.


3.  Flow conditions

	Re_tau = 150
	Re_b   = 4560
	Pr     = 0.71
	Cf     = 8.66E-3
	Nu     = 13.4

4.  Numerical data
